detail.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Separate MFSDP v2 module backward completion (`post_backward`) from parameter gradient completion (`post_accumulate_grad`). Shared invocations can release full weights before their shared gradients finish accumulating.

`post_backward` handles weight release and the module phase. A full-backward hook triggers it when input gradients arrive; otherwise the context runs it at autograd completion. The deferred-callback infrastructure, frozen-weight fix, scheduler callback registration, and frozen-weight regression are inherited from #8113. `post_accumulate_grad` packs and reduces gradients immediately when the existing parameter countdown or TE completion hooks report readiness. There is no pending-reduction flag or required ordering between the two callbacks. The combined-1F1B scheduler uses the gradient-completion registration too.

`post_backward()` uniformly frees full weight storage while retaining parameter bindings. `context.finish_grad_sync()` restores sharded bindings for every group, including frozen parameters. This keeps full-shaped bindings available for TE's delayed `.grad` assignment without a TE-specific branch or additional state. `post_accumulate_grad()` only packs and reduces gradients. Delayed wgrad without `caller_managed_grad_sync=True` is now rejected during hook registration.

Stacked on #8113 (`50e361943`), with GitHub base/diffbase `pull-request/8113`; #7854 has merged. The [prepared graph-counting follow-up](https://github.com/wujingyue/Megatron-LM/compare/90cf9109bf4a4eb494e9543fe2a65ff05be83f04...08c7c99f4b417af88d5d31d1333a0f0f5accfc2b) uses this separation and reduces zero-count units after backward setup. #7815's head/base remain unchanged until this draft has a `pull-request/7902` mirror.

Operation names distinguish parameter bindings from storage at both module and parameter-group levels:

- `unshard()`: materialize full weights and bind full parameters.
- `reshard()`: bind sharded parameters and release full weight storage (module-level composition).
- `bind_sharded_parameters()` / `bind_unsharded_parameters()`: change parameter references only.
- `release_unsharded_storage()`: free full storage without changing bindings.
- `reduce_gradients()`: reduce packed gradients at the parameter-group level. The module's `post_accumulate_grad()` lifecycle callback orchestrates packing and reduction.

The terminology cleanup passes formatting/lint and a syntax-tree equivalence check after normalizing renames and helper extraction; no training behavior changed or GPU tests were rerun for it.

## Validation and memory impact

The existing `test_delayed_wgrad_matches_immediate` now checks that full weight storage is released before every `backward_dw()` call; its training comparison supplies numerical coverage. The standalone delayed-wgrad test is removed. The updated adapter test **passed on all four NSC-LHR GB300 ranks** at `56190ee77` (job 154997). The rejection test and single shared-layer storage test passed in job 151715. Only the rejection test is added to `test_context.py`. Black, isort, pylint, Ruff, and `git diff --check` pass; mypy is unavailable.

Storage-release annotations (`d1c75b0e0`): the module emits one `release_unsharded_storage` range for each forward/backward release, replacing the enclosing `reshard` range. All **6 annotation tests passed per rank** on four NSC-LHR GB300 GPUs (job 151322). Formatting and lint checks pass; mypy is unavailable. Training logic is unchanged.

Rebased onto #8113 (`50e361943`) at `1d77fb425`. The full MFSDP v2 suite on four NSC-LHR GB300 GPUs passed: **262–263 passed, 1–2 skipped per rank** (job 150911). Black, isort, pylint, Ruff, and `git diff --check` pass; mypy is unavailable in the CI image. The three changed production files are AST-equivalent to the previous PR head after excluding docstrings. The duplicate frozen-weight test was removed because #8113 provides it.

Earlier validation and performance measurements follow, with their tested commits identified.

Binding-restoration simplification (`2ee672385`), four NSC-LHR GPUs: the full suite passed 260–261 tests per rank, with one failure in the old late-rejection test (job 140129). After moving that rejection to registration, all **7 delayed-wgrad, synchronization, and scheduler tests passed per rank** (job 140219). Formatting and lint checks pass; mypy is unavailable.

Rebased onto `origin/main` (`43ecc88de`) at `3ddd41d83`. Full MFSDP v2 suite on four NSC-LHR GB300 GPUs: **260–261 passed, 1–2 skipped per rank** (job 137822). Formatting and lint checks pass; mypy remains unavailable in the image.

Latest storage-lifetime fix (`123110b49`), four GB300 GPUs on NSC-LHR:

- Full MFSDP v2 suite: **257–258 passed, 1–2 skipped per rank** (job 118114).
- The extended delayed-wgrad regression fails on the previous head because all 512 weight bytes remain allocated. With the fix, storage is zero before `backward_dw()` and the reduced gradient matches an unsharded reference. Automatic synchronization still rejects delayed wgrad as required by #7854.
- Separate Linear and GroupedLinear probes in both BF16 and MXFP8 verify freed full-weight storage and matching reference gradients (job 118151).
- Black, isort, pylint, Ruff, and `git diff --check` pass; mypy is unavailable in the image.

The functional timing comparison below predates this storage-lifetime fix and remains labeled with its tested head, `90cf910`.

Two RTX A6000 GPUs in the development CI image:

- Full `tests/unit_tests/distributed/mfsdp_v2 --experimental`: **198 passed, 55 skipped per rank** on the callback split (`051e30af`).
- Scheduler-owned callback registration: **27 passed per rank**, covering context, annotation, checkpoint, frozen-parent, and shared-unit tests. The scheduler test checks both reduced gradients and deferred frozen-weight release.
- A small GPT model with two MTP depths sharing one TransformerLayer completed forward/backward on two GPUs, with finite gradients and all module phases returning to RESTING. Removing the `pre_backward()` guard reproduces `BACKWARD -> BACKWARD`: MTP passes grad-requiring hidden states by keyword, which the full backward hook does not track.
- Prepared graph-counting follow-up: **7 tests passed per rank** before the scheduler-only update; its graph-counting patch is unchanged.
- The existing eight-layer memory probe (4096×4096 BF16 weights) measured **96.17 MiB → 128.17 MiB** peak allocation above resting memory when removing the gate: **32 MiB**, one additional full buffer. Both ranks and both communication-stream configurations showed that result in this comparison. The test now budgets four full buffers; its previous unified-stream bound was three.
- Updated the NVTX assertion to show storage release after gradient reduction in this no-input-gradient case. Shared-layer, frozen-weight, checkpoint, delayed-TE, and manual-scheduler regressions passed in that earlier run.
- Black, isort, pylint, Ruff, and `git diff --check` pass. Mypy is unavailable in the image.

The memory measurement above is a small synthetic probe. Functional proxy measurements are below. Backward prefetch still uses static module order. Invocation-aware prefetch and shared reentrant checkpointing are outside this change.

**Known limitation:** PyTorch full backward hooks track positional tensor inputs only. MCore TransformerLayer calls pass `hidden_states` by keyword, so these units currently retain their full weights until the final callback even when their hidden states require gradients. This can increase full-model peak memory substantially; the positional-input memory probe above does not measure that effect. The shared-invocation guard remains necessary for repeated-layer MTP under this behavior.

## Functional performance comparison (NSC-LHR)

Compared baseline `dddd756` with PR head `90cf910` on GB300: seven existing 8-GPU functional configurations plus the existing 4-GPU MXFP8 configuration. **All 22 training runs completed 50 steps; every paired logged loss and peak-allocation value matched.** Training and optimizer CUDA graph capture both completed in the graph recipe.

**Scope:** this uses `MockGPTDataset` and `NullTokenizer` (50257 tokens), since the exact CI corpora could not be downloaded and reads of the shared copy timed out. Model, batch, and iteration settings are preserved. This is a paired performance comparison, not a CI corpus/golden-value pass.

**Common prerequisite:** both unmodified snapshots failed before training because `megatron/training/models/dist_utils.py` creates the shared context without `caller_managed_grad_sync=True`. Both benchmark copies receive that identical one-line setup correction. The PR branch itself is unchanged.

Step time is the median over iterations 11–50. Memory is the maximum TensorBoard `mem-max-allocated-bytes` on the CI logging rank, not a maximum across ranks. TensorBoard and rank logs are written locally and copied out after training. Each pair runs sequentially in the same allocation and container, using `_run_training.sh` with the torchrun launcher.

| Configuration | Baseline ms | PR ms | Change | Peak allocated GiB, baseline / PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek EP2 | 192.0 | 189.7 | -1.2% | 24.288 / 24.288 |
| DeepSeek EP2 + delayed wgrad | 228.9 | 228.3 | -0.3% | 24.505 / 24.505 |
| Llama-3 proxy + CUDA graphs | 20.8 | 20.6 | -1.0% | 4.183 / 4.183 |
| DeepSeek EP2, two microbatches | 285.2 | 288.1 | +1.0% | 24.290 / 24.290 |
| DeepSeek HSDP, two microbatches | 288.8 | 295.6 | +2.4% | 24.559 / 24.559 |
| DeepSeek HFSDP, two microbatches | 353.5 | 285.4 | -19.3% | 24.360 / 24.360 |
| DeepSeek HFSDP, two microbatches — reverse-order repeat | 311.6 | 311.5 | -0.0% | 24.360 / 24.360 |
| GPT CP2 | 284.2 | 243.9 | -14.2% | 1.247 / 1.247 |
| GPT CP2 — reverse-order repeat | 268.5 | 274.3 | +2.2% | 1.247 / 1.247 |
| DeepSeek MXFP8 (4 GPUs) | 399.3 | 422.8 | +5.9% | 23.199 / 23.199 |
| DeepSeek MXFP8 (4 GPUs) — reverse-order repeat | 402.7 | 402.9 | +0.0% | 23.199 / 23.199 |

The three large initial timing differences did not reproduce in reverse order. Those repeats differ by less than 0.1% for HFSDP/MXFP8 and +2.2% for GPT CP2; the other first-pass differences range from -1.2% to +2.4%. These short runs do not establish a tight throughput bound. Unchanged proxy peak allocation also does not remove the keyword-input retention limitation above.

Environment: PyTorch `2.14.0a0+4fdf77b940.nv26.08`, Transformer Engine `2.20.2+6ea2a74a`, NCCL `2.30.7`, driver `580.178.04`. Pinned development image digest: `sha256:2afed666dabe4e828fc5a160322a57733ecd4ffc065dce59c8671dc5009e471d`.

Completed NSC-LHR jobs: `109746` (original 8-GPU comparison), `109825` and `109880` (MXFP8 and its repeat), `110026` (HFSDP/GPT repeats on a second node pair). MXFP8 repeated on its original node. All allocations are released. Scripts, source archives, training logs, TensorBoard files, and exit-code verification are under `/scratch/fsw/portfolios/coreai/users/jingyuew/mfsdp-functional-7902-20261007` on NSC-LHR.

## Issue tracking

Related to #7764 and #7791. Depends on #8113, which fixes #7823. #7854 has merged.

## Contribution process

- [x] Added focused unit regressions.
- [x] Ran `tools/autoformat.sh` (mypy unavailable).
- [x] Ran existing functional training recipes with mock data (results and limitations above).
- [ ] GPU kernel determinism tests (not applicable: no kernel changes).
